newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's chief spy tenders resignation - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Romania's chief spy tenders resignation - spokesman.

text.p: The head of Romania's intelligence service, a key player in the 1989 anti-communist revolt, has offered to resign because of domestic and foreign "pressure", his spokesman said on Friday.

The spokesman, Nicolae Ulieru, told Bucharest radio that Virgil Magureanu tendered his resignation following "pressure by groups in Romania and abroad" on the new government to replace the heads of the country's intelligence services.
"This is not the time to give details," he said.
To become effective, the resignation must be approved by reformist President Emil Constantinescu.
Magureanu had said before last November's presidential election, in which Constantinescu defeated ex-communist Ion Iliescu, that he would quit regardless of the outcome.

But Ulieru did not deny reports in Bucharest newspapers that diplomats had suggested that Magureanu's departure would help Romania's remote chances to win early admission to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
"Probably yes," Ulieru said when asked to comment if the resignation was related to the NATO issue.
Romania has launched a high-profile diplomatic offensive since November to be included in NATO's first expansion wave in July alongside favoured Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
A former officer in the communist-era Securitate secret police, Magureanu is the only leading figure of the December 1989 revolt that ousted dictator Nicolae Ceausescu to have kept his original job.
He appeared on television as a member of the jury which sentenced Ceausescu and his wife Elena to death on Christmas Day 1989.

Many liberals saw the revolt as a palace coup masterminded by the Securitate along with second-rank communists, including Iliescu, who emerged as the country's leader and was later twice elected president.

In his interview, Ulieru defended the SRI as an institution which "uses modern methods, perfectly compatible with the demands of democracy and the state of law". Magureanu's resignation offer, he said, was a "strictly personal gesture".
The SRI was created in 1990 under a presidential decree signed by Iliescu. But neither Magureanu's appointment nor the decree was published in the Official Gazette.
